questions.text: How does a transcutaneous monitor differ from a standard pulse oximeter?

answers.text: It measures both PtcO₂ and PtcCO₂ and heats the skin to arterialize the underlying capillaries
It measures only oxygen saturation but with greater accuracy
It requires a continuous arterial blood draw to function
It cools the skin to slow metabolism at the sensor site

questions.text: Why must a transcutaneous electrode be repositioned every 2–6 hours?

answers.text: To prevent thermal damage to the skin from the heating element
To recalibrate the oxygen saturation reading
Because the adhesive loses its seal after 2 hours
To alternate between measuring O₂ and CO₂

questions.text: Inhaled nitric oxide improves oxygenation in PPHN by which mechanism?

answers.text: It is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that dilates constricted capillaries around healthy alveoli, overcoming shunt
It is a systemic vasoconstrictor that raises blood pressure
It directly increases surfactant production in type II cells
It bronchodilates the small airways to reduce resistance

questions.text: When weaning a patient off inhaled nitric oxide, why should FiO₂ be increased as the iNO is decreased?

answers.text: To prevent rebound hypoxemia and a return to PPHN
To keep nitrogen dioxide levels above 2 PPM
To raise methemoglobin above 5% of total hemoglobin
Because FiO₂ has no relationship to nitric oxide weaning

questions.text: A neonate requires both cardiac and pulmonary support on ECMO. Which configuration is appropriate, and how is it cannulated?

answers.text: VA (veno-arterial) ECMO — right internal jugular vein to the right atrium, and the right common carotid artery to the aortic arch
VV (veno-venous) ECMO — right internal jugular vein and right femoral vein
VV ECMO — because it provides the most cardiac support
VA ECMO — cannulating only the right femoral vein

questions.text: Which device is the standard unit in the delivery room because it provides an open environment to manipulate the patient and perform CPR?

answers.text: The radiant warmer
The closed incubator/isolette
The oxyhood
The bubble CPAP setup

questions.text: Using the formula Tube ID = (Age + 16) / 4, what is the appropriate uncuffed ETT internal diameter for a 4-year-old child?

answers.text: 5.0 mm
4.0 mm
6.0 mm
3.5 mm

questions.text: A pediatric patient is placed on a simple mask. What minimum flow is needed, and what happens below 5 L/min?

answers.text: Greater than 10 L/min is satisfactory; less than 5 L/min causes CO₂ rebreathing
Greater than 2 L/min is satisfactory; less than 1 L/min causes CO₂ rebreathing
Any flow is adequate because the mask stores oxygen between breaths
Greater than 15 L/min is required to avoid pressure necrosis

questions.text: An infant has a small tidal volume and needs a bronchodilator. How is the medication best delivered?

answers.text: By bagging in the medication with a spacer and Jackson-Reese bag, or via an inline Aerogen if ventilated
With a standard adult facemask and SVN
By instilling the liquid medication directly down the ETT
Only through a metered-dose inhaler held to the face

questions.text: An air/oxygen blender suddenly emits a harmonic sound. What does this indicate, and what should be done to confirm the delivered FiO₂?

answers.text: A gas source has failed; confirm the FiO₂ with an O₂ analyzer
The proportioning valve is working normally; no action is needed
The patient is over-oxygenated; lower the flow immediately
The blender is calibrated; document the set FiO₂ as accurate
